'''Chikezie Jake''' "'''KZ'''" '''Okpala'''{{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Obefelix-Chikezie Jake Okpala.wav|Listen|help=no}}<ref name="fitzgerald">{{cite web |last1=FitzGerald |first1=Tom |title=Late-bloomer KZ Okpala is growing his game at Stanford |url=https://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Late-bloomer-KZ-Okpala-is-growing-his-game-at-12560060.php |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> (born April 28, 1999) is an American-Nigerian former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]].

==Early life==
Okpala was born to Nigerian parents Martin and Mary Okpala, who settled in [[Orange County, California]] before his birth.<ref name="fryer">{{cite web |last1=Fryer |first1=Steve |title=Esperanza's Kezie Okpala is the Register's 2016-17 boys basketball player of the year |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2017/04/04/esperanzas-kezie-okpala-is-the-registers-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=January 13, 2019 |date=April 4, 2017}}</ref> He began playing basketball at age 4 but did not join a youth league because he found them unruly.<ref name=fitzgerald/> Okpala grew up playing the game against adults at [[Health club|fitness]] clubs and parks.<ref name="rosy">{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=On high schools: Late bloomer KZ Okpala of Esperanza has a rosy future |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-kz-okpala-esperanza-20170119-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=January 19, 2017}}</ref> When he was in fourth grade, his family moved from [[Fresno, California|Fresno]] back to Orange County, living in [[Yorba Linda, California|Yorba Linda]], where he reached out to a local club team.<ref name=fitzgerald/> Okpala also played [[American football|football]] and [[baseball]] in his childhood before focusing on basketball by age 11.<ref name=fryer/>

==High school career==
Okpala attended [[Esperanza High School]] in [[Anaheim, California]]. He grew from {{height|ft=5|in=10}} to {{height|ft=6|in=8}} during his four years playing high school basketball.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=KZ Okpala |url=https://gostanford.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=14132 |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=January 14, 2019}}</ref> Okpala joined the starting lineup as a sophomore.<ref name=lead>{{cite web |last1=Fryer |first1=Steve |title=Esperanza's Okpala ready to lead |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2016/11/27/boys-basketball-preview-esperanzas-okpala-ready-to-lead/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=November 27, 2016}}</ref> On January 16, 2015, during that season, he made a buzzer-beating three-pointer to defeat [[El Dorado High School (Placentia, California)|El Dorado High School]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Connolly |first1=Kenny |title=Okpala's shot gives Esperanza dramatic win |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2015/01/16/okpalas-shot-gives-esperanza-dramatic-win/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> As a junior, Okpala averaged 23 points and 8 rebounds per game to lead Esperanza to a conference title and win Crestview League Player of the Year honors. His most notable moment in that year was when Okpala dunked on Trevor Hooks of Orange High School.<ref name=lead/>

In his senior season, he improved to 30 points, 11 rebounds, and 2 blocks per game.<ref name=bio/> On November 25, 2016, Okpala tallied 41 points in a 76–59 win over [[Spartanburg Day School]] at the Tournament of Champions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Regan |first1=Brett |title=Kezie Okpala's Impressive 41 Outshines Zion Williamson |url=https://www.flohoops.com/articles/5058112-kezie-okpalas-impressive-41-outshines-zion-williamson |publisher=FloHoops |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=November 25, 2016}}</ref> He scored a career-high 46 points against [[Crossroads School (Santa Monica, California)|Crossroads School]], which set a school record.<ref name=bio/><ref name="lateam">{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=The all-Los Angeles Times boys' basketball team for 2017 |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-all-latimes-boys-20170328-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=March 28, 2017}}</ref> On March 26, 2017, Okpala led Esperanza to its first [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) Division II championship, scoring 22 points versus [[Moreau Catholic High School]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Esperanza boys capture state Division II basketball title |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2017/03/26/esperanza-boys-capture-state-division-ii-basketball-title/ |website=[[Orange County Register]] |access-date=January 14, 2019|date=March 26, 2017}}</ref> He was named Crestview League Player of the Year and played at the [[Ballislife All-American Game]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kezie Okpala |url=http://www.ballislifeallamerican.com/2017alum/kezie-okpala-68-small-forward/ |publisher=[[Ballislife All-American Game]] |access-date=January 14, 2019}}</ref>

Okpala was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top high school players in California.<ref name="rivals">{{cite web |title=Kezie Okpala, 2017 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/kezie-okpala-182070 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 14, 2019}}</ref><ref name="247sports">{{cite web |title=KZ Okpala, Esperanza, Small Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/KZ-Okpala-89068/high-school-170859/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 14, 2019}}</ref> He received an offer from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] in July 2016, shortly before committing there.<ref name=rivals/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Drukarev |first1=Andy |title=Okpala receives Stanford offer, plans trip |url=https://stanford.rivals.com/news/okpala-receives-stanford-offer-plans-trip |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=August 1, 2016 |archive-date=May 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526095317/https://stanford.rivals.com/news/okpala-receives-stanford-offer-plans-trip |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Okpala missed his first 11 games of his freshman season at Stanford because of academic ineligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Stanford freshman forward Kezie Okpala to sit out due to academics |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21368196/stanford-cardinal-freshman-kezie-okpala-sit-due-academics |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=November 10, 2017}}</ref> On December 21, 2017, after being cleared to play, he debuted with 6 points in 28 minutes against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shook |first1=Nick |title=Highly touted freshman Kezie Okpala cleared to play for Stanford |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/college/report-highly-touted-freshman-kezie-okpala-cleared-play-for-stanford/lUjTNV1EmRx0eyq1RT394M/ |website=[[Dayton Daily News]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=December 21, 2017 }}{{Dead link|date=February 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dec 21, 2017 - Stanford 54 at Kansas 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2017-12-21/Stanford-at-Kansas/277837 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=December 21, 2017}}</ref> On March 3, 2018, Okpala recorded his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]], tallying 18 points and 10 rebounds in an 84–83 win over [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 19 Arizona pulls away late to beat California |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/more/la-sp-pac-12-basketball-20180303-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> He scored a season-high 23 points on March 8, in an 88–77 loss to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mar 8, 2018 - Stanford 77 at UCLA 88 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2018-03-08/Stanford-at-UCLA/293529 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}}</ref> As a freshman, Okpala averaged 10 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.<ref name=bio/>

On November 6, 2018, he made his sophomore debut with 29 points, 10 rebounds, and 5 assists in a 96–74 win over [[Seattle Redhawks men's basketball|Seattle]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=FitzGerald |first1=Tom |title=KZ Okpala hits career-high 29 points as Stanford rips Seattle in opener |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/Okpala-hits-career-high-29-points-as-Stanford-13369567.php |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=November 6, 2018}}</ref> Six days later, Okpala earned [[Pac-12 Conference]] player of the week recognition.<ref>{{cite web |title=Okpala Honored |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2018/11/12/mens-basketball-okpala-honored.aspx |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=November 12, 2018}}</ref> On January 9, 2019, he had another strong performance, erupting for 29 points, 6 rebounds, and 4 assists against [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eymer |first1=Rick |title=A great effort goes unrewarded for Stanford men's hoops |url=https://www.paloaltoonline.com/news/2019/01/09/a-great-effort-goes-unrewarded-for-stanford-mens-hoops |website=[[Palo Alto Weekly]] |access-date=January 14, 2019 |date=January 9, 2019}}</ref>

At the conclusion of his sophomore season, Okpala announced his intention to forgo his final two seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26497866/stanford-okpala-enters-draft-chase-dream|title=Stanford's Okpala enters draft to chase 'dream'|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 11, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Miami Heat (2019–2022)===
Okpala was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 32nd overall pick in the 2019 NBA draft but was soon after traded to the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-draft-rights-kz-okpala|title=HEAT Acquire The Draft Rights To KZ Okpala|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019}}</ref> On July 7, 2019, [[Miami Heat]] announced that they had signed Okpala to a three-year, $4.2 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kz-okpala-190707|title=HEAT Signs KZ Okpala|date=July 7, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> He played in two of the Heat's first four games, but missed 19 games due to an Achilles strain. In December 2019, Okpala was assigned to the Heat's G League affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. He averaged 11.7 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.1 blocks per game in 20 appearances with the Skyforce.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Winderman |first1=Ira |title=KZ Okpala working for respect, as Heat take long view with 2019 second-round pick |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-kz-okpala-development-20200531-hprlhsvtobg3heb3j677vge3xq-story.html |access-date=June 14, 2020 |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |date=May 31, 2020}}</ref>

On August 1, 2021, Okpala joined the Heat for the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}}</ref>

On February 9, 2022, Okpala was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for draft considerations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires KZ Okpala and Amends Conditions of First Round Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-okpala-220209|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2022|access-date=February 9, 2022}}</ref> He was waived two days later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thunder Waives KZ Okpala|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-okpala-220211|access-date=February 11, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2022–2023)===
On September 14, 2022, Okpala signed a two-year, $4 million contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kings Sign KZ Okpala|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-kz-okpala|date=September 14, 2022|website=NBA.com}}</ref> On February 25, 2023, Okpala was waived.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/02/kings-to-waive-kz-okpala-bring-back-pj-dozier.html|title=Kings To Waive KZ Okpala, Bring Back PJ Dozier|website=hoopsrumors.com|date=February 25, 2023|access-date=February 25, 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
Okpala played for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national basketball team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=KZ Okpala (Nigeria) |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/300686-kz-okpala |website=FIBA |access-date=December 11, 2024}}</ref>
